title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting bug had Saudi support, claims prosecutors

claims.claim: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi national and former OpenAI worker, was charged with secretly planting a recording device in an OpenAI meeting room.

evidence.quote: A Saudi national charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's meeting rooms has been accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government, according to a court filing, external in California.
US prosecutors claimed Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked for the ChatGPT-maker, was in "frequent communication... with a member of the Saudi royal family"
A Saudi national charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's meeting rooms has been accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government

claims.claim: Prosecutors claimed Alfozan had considerable support from the Saudi government and was in frequent communication with a member of the Saudi royal family.

evidence.quote: A Saudi national charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's meeting rooms has been accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government, according to a court filing, external in California.

A Saudi national charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's meeting rooms has been accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government, according to a court filing, external in California. US prosecutors claimed Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked for the ChatGPT-maker, was in "frequent communication... with a member of the Saudi royal family"

claims.claim: The 35-year-old engineer was denied bail on Monday by US district judge Alex Tse, pending a trial.

evidence.quote: The 35-year-old engineer was deemed a flight risk and denied bail on Monday, pending a trial.
US district judge Alex Tse on Monday denied Alfozan's attorneys request for his release on bail, saying "there is a risk of non-appearance that is significant".
US district judge Alex Tse on Monday denied Alfozan's attorneys request for his release on bail

claims.claim: OpenAI discovered the audio recording device, plugged into the back of a TV in a conference meeting room and covered with toilet paper, on 30 September.

evidence.quote: The AI company discovered the device, which was plugged into the back of a TV in a conference meeting room and covered up with toilet paper, on 30 September.

claims.claim: Alfozan was filmed by a camera placed in the room entering and appearing to look behind the television on 5 October.

evidence.quote: A camera was placed in the room and on 5 October, Alfozan was filmed entering and appearing to look behind the television where the audio recorder had been inserted.

claims.claim: Alfozan was arrested by the FBI on 9 October and his contract with OpenAI was terminated.

evidence.quote: He was arrested by the FBI on 9 October and his contract with OpenAI was terminated.

claims.claim: On 10 October, Alfozan's wife and son flew from San Francisco to Doha, Qatar, on a one-way business class ticket paid for by a Saudi military official.

evidence.quote: On 10 October, the day after Alfozan was arrested, his wife and son flew from San Francisco to Doha, Qatar. They travelled on a one-way business class ticket booked and paid for by a Saudi military official.

claims.claim: If convicted, Alfozan faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

evidence.quote: If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 (Â£188,000) fine.
